loci.textAr: إِشَارَةٌ بِأَنَّ العَبْدَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُرَاعِيَ الشَّرِيعَةَ وَالحَقِيقَةَ: ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ﴾ شَرِيعَةٌ وَ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ﴾ حَقِيقَةٌ
loci.textEn: An indication that the servant must observe both the Law and the Reality: Thee do we worship is Law, and Thee do we ask for help is Reality.

loci.textAr: إِنَّ العَرْشَ مَقْلُوبُ شَرْعٍ… فَالشَّرْعُ مَجْمُوعُ رَحْمَةِ الأَرْضِ وَمَحَطُّهَا
loci.textEn: The Throne (ʿarsh) is sharʿ inverted… so the Law is the sum of the earth's mercy and its landing-place.

loci.textAr: يَكْفِي المَرْءَ مِنْ عِلْمِ الكَلَامِ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾ مِنْ تَوْحِيدِ الأَفْعَالِ وَالصِّفَاتِ وَالذَّاتِ
loci.textEn: This one verse suffices a man in place of dialectical theology — on the oneness of acts, of attributes, and of the essence.

loci.textAr: النُّورُ أَقْسَامٌ أَرْبَعَةٌ: نُورٌ يُرِيكَ وَلَا يُرَى، وَنُورٌ يُرِيكَ وَيُرَى كَنُورِ العَيْنِ، وَنُورٌ يُرِيكَ فَقَطْ كَنُورِ العَقْلِ، وَنُورٌ يُرِيكَ المَوْجُودَ وَيُرِيكَ المَعْدُومَ وَهُوَ ﴿اللهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ﴾. مَثَّلَ قَلْبَ المُؤْمِنِ بِالزُّجَاجَةِ تَعْلِيمًا لَكَ… فَالزُّجَاجَةُ سَرِيعَةُ الاِنْكِسَارِ وَهَكَذَا القَلْبُ، فَاحْتَفِظْ عَلَيْهِ جِدًّا
loci.textEn: Light is of four kinds: a light that shows you and is not itself seen; a light that shows you and is seen, like the light of the eye; a light that only shows you, like the light of the intellect; and a light that shows you the existent and shows you the non-existent — and that is God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. He likened the believer's heart to the glass as a lesson to you… glass breaks quickly, and so does the heart. Guard it well.

loci.textAr: لَا يُمْكِنُ لِلنَّفْسِ الاِطْمِئْنَانُ إِلَّا بِالمَعْرِفَةِ. أَمَّا نُفُوسُ أَهْلِ الدُّنْيَا فَلَا تَطْمَئِنُّ، لِأَنَّهَا دَائِمَةٌ حَرِيصَةٌ فِي الطَّلَبِ
loci.textEn: The soul cannot come to rest except through gnosis. The souls of worldly people never rest, because they are perpetually avid in pursuit.

The bāʾ of the basmala: the dot beneath the alif, tawāḍuʿ and rafʿ — man tawāḍaʿa rafaʿahu llāh. Hadith: mā bayna bismillāh al-raḥmān al-raḥīm wa-bayna al-ism al-aʿẓam illā kamā bayna sawād al-ʿayn wa-bayāḍihā.

Aqsām al-ḥamd; rabb al-ʿālamīn — al-ʿālam is everything other than God; the masculine plural by taghlīb. al-Rabb is the one who rears, whether by small favours or by great ones — ʿulūm, maʿārif, laṭāʾif, asrār.
al-Raḥīm: raḥma as riqqat al-qalb is impossible of God; its terminus, tafaḍḍul, is not. Hadith of the hundred mercies.
mālik yawm al-dīn — kings of this world are contested; He is not.

Taqdīm al-mafʿūl li-l-ḥaṣr. THE KEY DIVISION: iyyāka naʿbudu = sharīʿa, wa-iyyāka nastaʿīnu = ḥaqīqa. Then ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib on riyāʾ — ṣallaytu al-bāriḥa miʾat rakʿa. Collate against Fī Riyāḍ Lesson 1.

God did not say ṣirāṭ alladhīna qutilū wa-dhubiḥū. The objection from the four caliphs, all martyred though all prayed for ʿāfiya. Resolution: al-ʿāfiya huwa al-riḍā bi-l-qadar — not that the Master assist you in all you desire, but that you consent to every decree. al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim = the Jews, al-ḍāllīn = the Christians. NOTE the parallel four-caliphs excursus in Fī Riyāḍ vol. 1, pp. 56-59, on Q 2:3 (Wright 2024).

al-Raḥmān ʿalā l-ʿarsh istawā — inna l-ʿarsh maqlūb sharʿ: the consonants of ʿ-r-sh reversed give sh-r-ʿ. The Throne is where God's mercy descends, so the Law is the sum and landing-place of mercy on earth. NO PARALLEL FOUND in the published scholarship on Niasse.

hiya ʿaṣāya — al-ʿaṣā and al-maʿṣiya are cognate in the lafẓ: what the servant ascribes to himself becomes a living thing against him. Then Moses' tongue, the coal, and why the miracle required the earlier defect.
law kāna fīhimā ālihatun illā llāhu la-fasadatā — ʿilm al-kalām is blamed and an innovation, and this one verse suffices a man, on tawḥīd al-afʿāl wa-l-ṣifāt wa-l-dhāt.
wa-jaʿalnā min al-māʾ kulla shayʾin ḥayy — as water is the cause of every living thing here, lā ilāha illā llāh is the cause of life hereafter; that word is the water of the next world.

Taṣrīḥ against taʿrīḍ in supplication: Zachariah asks explicitly (rabbi hab lī min ladunka waliyyan) because he seeks a good; Job alludes (annī massaniya l-ḍurr) because he seeks the lifting of an affliction, and allusion is nearer to adab.

wa-lā tulhikum amwālukum wa-lā awlādukum ʿan dhikri llāh — whoever is not connected to the Presence is, ʿinda ahl al-ḥaqīqa, ibn zinan. Also the four gazes that count as worship: the Kaʿba, a parent's face, the muṣḥaf, a scholar's face.

FOUR LIGHTS: that which shows you and is not seen; that which shows you and is seen (the eye's light); that which only shows you (the intellect's light); and that which shows you the existent AND the non-existent — and that is God. Then the zujāja as the believer's heart: glass breaks fast; too much sleep, food and mixing with worldly people clouds it. COLLATION TARGET — Wright 2024 cites Fī Riyāḍ vol. 4, pp. 217-218 on this verse but does not analyse it.
man yamshī ʿalā baṭnih = appetite of the belly; on two feet = appetite of sex; on four = those who seek jāh, called four because they are ridden. And some of the ʿārifūn walk by their spirits.

li-yaghfira laka llāhu — the agent is not repeated; God assigns the act to Himself. The Prophet being maʿṣūm, the maghfira returns to the umma (cf. li-yudkhila l-muʾminīn). Three things no veil stops: a parent's prayer for a child, the prayer of the wronged, the word of ikhlāṣ.
wa-mā ṣabruka illā bi-llāh; wa-mā l-naṣru illā min ʿind Allāh; in yanṣurkumu llāhu fa-lā ghāliba lakum. 'Nowhere in the Qurʾān is victory mentioned without God being made its agent.'

alḥaqnā bihim dhurriyyatahum — the murīd of deficient state is joined to his shaykh's station as the child of deficient faith is joined to the parent's. al-marʾ maʿa man aḥabb.
kulla yawmin huwa fī shaʾn — the boy who answered from the floor and was raised to the minbar; he was Mālik b. Anas.
laʿib / lahw / zīna / tafākhur / takāthur mapped onto the seven-year ages of a life. Whoever has not repented to God by thirty is al-maghbūn.
fīhi baʾsun shadīdun wa-manāfiʿu li-l-nās — what is of general benefit God made cheap (iron, fresh water, air); what has no use He made dear (gold, musk). 'Thus God exchanged, out of His mercy.'
kallā innahum ʿan rabbihim yawmaʾidhin la-maḥjūbūn — the veil is the CAUSE of the punishment, as a sultan first screens himself from the man he means to punish.

yā ayyatuhā l-nafsu l-muṭmaʾinna — lā yumkin li-l-nafs al-iṭmiʾnān illā bi-l-maʿrifa. The souls of worldly people never rest: desire in pursuit cannot rest, desire in possession fears loss. WRIGHT'S 2024 THESIS (maʿrifa bi-llāh as the telos of Niasse's exegesis) stated flatly in 1956, on a verse he does not treat, in a text he does not know.

aḥad indefinite because His unicity is hidden from creation save from ahl al-maʿrifa; al-Ṣamad definite because known even to the deniers (Q 29:61). lam yalid wa-lam yūlad negates being begotten BEFORE begetting, since the deniers claimed the latter and none claimed the former (Q 9:30; the Arab pagans on the angels). Then: aḥad is the trustee (amīn) the intellect seeks, al-Ṣamad the rich man (ghanī muthrī) desire seeks.
Cited within the al-Ikhlāṣ commentary.
Cited within the al-Ikhlāṣ commentary.

qul aʿūdhu bi-rabb al-falaq — ONE name only (al-Rabb), because refuge is sought from four worldly harms and the need is worldly. ʿālam al-khalq (dense bodies) against ʿālam al-amr (luminous spirits, angels), from which no harm issues at all.

THREE names — rabb, malik, ilāh — because the need is religious. al-Rabb for the small, who need tarbiya and iṣlāḥ; al-Malik for the young, whose strength must be curbed by a king they cannot resist; al-Ilāh for the old, who have nothing left but return. Fa-l-nās thalāthat aqsām.
al-Ikhlāṣ is a third of the Qurʾān because the Qurʾān is command and prohibition, outward and inward, and ikhlāṣ is tawḥīd entire; al-Kāfirūn a quarter, negating worship of any other.
